title: Static Routing Across Two Subnets Lab
objective: Connect two distinct local area networks via two Cisco routers (R1 and R2), configure static IPv4 routes, and verify end-to-end communication across routers.

configurations.R1:
enable
configure terminal
hostname R1

interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 description LAN 1 Gateway
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
exit

interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 description WAN link to R2
 ip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.252
 no shutdown
exit

ip route 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2

end
write memory
configurations.R2:
enable
configure terminal
hostname R2

interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 description LAN 2 Gateway
 ip address 192.168.2.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
exit

interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 description WAN link to R1
 ip address 10.0.0.2 255.255.255.252
 no shutdown
exit

ip route 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.1

end
write memory
configurations.SW1:
enable
configure terminal
hostname SW1
! Layer 2 switch forwarding traffic for LAN 1 on default VLAN 1
end
write memory
configurations.SW2:
enable
configure terminal
hostname SW2
! Layer 2 switch forwarding traffic for LAN 2 on default VLAN 1
end
write memory

instructions: Place two Cisco 2911 Routers (R1, R2), two Cisco 2960 Switches (SW1, SW2), and four PCs (PC1, PC2 in LAN 1, PC3, PC4 in LAN 2).
Connect LAN 1: PC1 (Fa0) -> SW1 (Fa0/1), PC2 (Fa0) -> SW1 (Fa0/2), SW1 (Gi0/1) -> R1 (Gi0/0) using Straight-Through cables.
Connect WAN Link: R1 (Gi0/1) -> R2 (Gi0/1) using a Crossover or Straight-Through cable.
Connect LAN 2: R2 (Gi0/0) -> SW2 (Gi0/1), SW2 (Fa0/1) -> PC3 (Fa0), SW2 (Fa0/2) -> PC4 (Fa0).
Configure PC IP addresses, subnet masks, and Default Gateways as specified in the addressing table.
Open R1 CLI, answer 'no' to initial configuration dialog if prompted, and paste R1 commands.
Open R2 CLI, answer 'no' to initial configuration dialog if prompted, and paste R2 commands.
Ensure both router interfaces turn green (no shutdown applied).
verification: From PC1 Command Prompt, ping the local gateway: 'ping 192.168.1.1' (Expected: Success).
On R1 CLI, ping R2 WAN interface: 'ping 10.0.0.2' (Expected: 5/5 exclamation marks '!!!!!').
On R1 CLI, view routing table: 'show ip route' (Expected: 'S 192.168.2.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.0.2').
On R2 CLI, view routing table: 'show ip route' (Expected: 'S 192.168.1.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.0.1').
From PC1 Command Prompt, ping remote PC3: 'ping 192.168.2.10' (Expected: Success, first packet may time out during ARP resolution, subsequent packets reply).
